newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Macintosh sees second half net around nil.
newsitem.headline: Macintosh sees second half net around nil.

text.p: Dutch retail group Macintosh NV said on Monday it anticipated second half net profit would be around nil, mainly as a result of losses from its predominantly Belgian-based Superconfex clothing unit.
"The net profit over the second half year is expected to be around nil," the company said in a statement.
Company secretary Pat Hunen said by telephone that Superconfex had been making losses for around a year but declined to give details.
He said the poor performance of Superconfex in Belgium was the main reason for the profit warning, as well as an impact from Belgian tax laws which do not allow tax loss relief.

Macintosh said second half operating profit would, despite the expected contribution from the traditionally important December period, on current expectations lag the year ago period by around 50 percent, as it did in the first half this year.
In August Macintosh announced first half net profit slumped to 2.3 million guilders from 10.3 with operating profit down to 6.4 million from 12.5.
In 1995 the company had 22.5 million net profit, down from 38.5 million, while operating profit was 28.9 million guilders, down from 34.4 million.
Macintosh said the measures taken in 1996 would lead to a "clear" improvement in the net profit for 1997, without giving further details.
Superconfex sells family clothing with a network of some 70 shops in Belgium and 10 in the Netherlands.
